Read /tmp/audit/README_AUDIT.md FIRST for environment/ground-truth locations, and
/tmp/audit/spec.md for the project specification the implementation must satisfy.

The implementation under review is /workspace (src layout, package "fsutil").
Test it with:  PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src python3 ...
Upstream reference impls: /tmp/ref015/fsutil, /tmp/ref016/src/fsutil, /tmp/ref017/src/fsutil
Official test suites: /tmp/ref0{15,16,17}/tests  (ALL currently pass against /workspace)

HARD RULES:
- NEVER modify anything under /workspace. Read-only. Scratch files go in /tmp only.
- Verify every claim by ACTUALLY RUNNING python code. A finding you did not reproduce
  by execution does not count.
- The grading test suite is hidden. It is most likely the upstream tests for one of these
  versions, possibly with extra tests derived from the spec's documented signatures.
  So the highest-value findings are: things that would break a plausible hidden test.
- Do NOT report style nits, missing docstrings, or "consider adding". Only defects.

DIMENSION: API surface completeness & signature compatibility.
Enumerate EVERY function/name mentioned in /tmp/audit/spec.md and programmatically assert
that it is (a) importable from the top-level "fsutil" package, (b) importable from the
specific submodule the spec names, (c) callable with the EXACT positional and keyword
argument forms the spec documents (use inspect.signature and actual calls with positional
args). Also check fsutil.metadata exports and fsutil.__version__.
Write a script that loops over the whole documented API and reports every mismatch.
Report anything missing, misnamed, or that rejects a spec-documented call form.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# python-fsutil — project specification (verbatim requirements extract)
2	
3	The project is a Python library `fsutil` (distribution name `python-fsutil`) providing
4	high-level file-system operations. Required repo layout:
5	
6	```
7	workspace/
8	├── .gitignore
9	├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
10	├── CHANGELOG.md
11	├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
12	├── LICENSE.txt
13	├── MANIFEST.in
14	├── README.md
15	├── SECURITY.md
16	├── pyproject.toml
17	├── src/fsutil/{__init__,archives,args,checks,converters,deps,info,io,metadata,operations,paths,perms,types}.py
18	├── src/fsutil/py.typed
19	└── tox.ini
20	```
21	
22	Python >= 3.10 (env is 3.12.4). pyproject.toml must configure an installable package
23	(pip install AND editable mode), declare pytest (test) and requests (runtime) deps, and
24	specify the supported Python version range. MANIFEST.in must package metadata files,
25	type hints (py.typed) and all core modules.
26	
27	`src/fsutil/__init__.py` must be a unified API entry importing:
28	- archives: create_zip_file, extract_zip_file, create_tar_file, extract_tar_file
29	- checks: exists, is_file, is_dir, is_empty
30	- converters: convert_size_bytes_to_string, convert_size_string_to_bytes
31	- info: get_file_size, get_file_hash, get_dir_size, get_file_creation_date
32	- io: create_file, read_file, write_file, read_file_lines, list_files
33	- operations: copy_dir, copy_dir_content, delete_dir, delete_dir_content, clean_dir,
34	  make_dirs, remove_dir_content, create_dir, get_unique_name
35	- paths: join_path, split_filename, get_file_basename, get_file_extension, get_filename,
36	  get_parent_dir, join_filename, join_filepath, split_filepath, transform_filepath,
37	  split_path, get_path
38	- perms: get_permissions, set_permissions
39	- metadata: author/version etc.  (expose fsutil.__version__)
40	- args: get_path
41	- deps: require_requests
42	- exceptions: FSUtilError exception class
43	
44	`import fsutil` must give access to all major functions.
45	
46	## Documented API signatures (from the spec)
47	
48	```python
49	fsutil.create_file(path, content="", overwrite=False)
50	fsutil.copy_file(path, dest, overwrite=False, **kwargs)
51	fsutil.move_file(path, dest, overwrite=False, **kwargs)
52	fsutil.delete_file(path);  fsutil.remove_file(path)
53	fsutil.rename_file(path, name)
54	fsutil.rename_file_basename(path, basename)
55	fsutil.rename_file_extension(path, extension)
56	fsutil.replace_file(path, src, autodelete=False)
57	
58	fsutil.create_dir(path, overwrite=False)
59	fsutil.make_dirs(path);  fsutil.make_dirs_for_file(path)
60	fsutil.copy_dir(path, dest, overwrite=False, **kwargs)
61	fsutil.copy_dir_content(path, dest, **kwargs)
62	fsutil.move_dir(path, dest, overwrite=False, **kwargs)
63	fsutil.delete_dir(path);  fsutil.remove_dir(path)
64	fsutil.delete_dirs(*paths);  fsutil.remove_dirs(*paths)
65	fsutil.rename_dir(path, name)
66	fsutil.replace_dir(path, src, autodelete=False)
67	fsutil.clean_dir(path, dirs=True, files=True)
68	fsutil.delete_dir_content(path);  fsutil.remove_dir_content(path)
69	
70	fsutil.join_path(path, *paths)
71	fsutil.join_filepath(dirpath, filename)
72	fsutil.join_filename(basename, extension)
73	fsutil.split_path(path);  fsutil.split_filepath(path);  fsutil.split_filename(path)
74	fsutil.get_filename(path);  fsutil.get_file_basename(path);  fsutil.get_file_extension(path)

103	                       ensure_ascii=True, check_circular=True, allow_nan=True, cls=None,
104	                       indent=None, separators=None, default=None, sort_keys=False)
105	fsutil.read_file_from_url(url, **kwargs)
106	fsutil.download_file(url, dirpath=None, filename="archive.zip", chunk_size=8192, **kwargs)
107	
108	fsutil.create_zip_file(path, content_paths, overwrite=True, compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
109	fsutil.extract_zip_file(path, dest, content_paths=None, autodelete=False)
110	fsutil.create_tar_file(path, content_paths, overwrite=True, compression="gzip")
111	fsutil.extract_tar_file(path, dest, content_paths=None, autodelete=False)
112	
113	fsutil.get_permissions(path);  fsutil.set_permissions(path, 700)
114	fsutil.convert_size_bytes_to_string(size);  fsutil.convert_size_string_to_bytes(size)
115	fsutil.list_dirs(path);  fsutil.list_files(path)
116	fsutil.search_dirs(path, pattern="**/*");  fsutil.search_files(path, pattern="**/*.*")
117	```

119	Metadata importable from fsutil.metadata: __author__, __copyright__, __description__,
120	__email__, __license__, __title__, __version__
121	
122	## Documented behaviour examples from the spec
123	
124	- `fsutil.convert_size_bytes_to_string(1536)` -> `"1.5 KB"` (spec prose; note the real
125	  library and its official tests render `1536` as `"2 KB"`/2-decimals rules — the official
126	  test suite is authoritative)
127	- `fsutil.convert_size_string_to_bytes("2.5 MB")` -> `2621440`
128	- `basename, ext = fsutil.split_filename("document.pdf")`
129	- `dir_path, filename = fsutil.split_filepath("/home/user/document.pdf")`
130	- `fsutil.get_parent_dir("/home/user/documents/file.txt", levels=2)`
131	- `fsutil.set_permissions("script.sh", 0o755)` and `fsutil.set_permissions("script.sh", 755)`
132	- `fsutil.get_permissions("script.sh")` then `oct(permissions)`
133	- error handling: copying a nonexistent file should be catchable as FileNotFoundError /
134	  PermissionError / generic Exception
135	- atomic writes via `atomic=True`; append via `append=True`
136	- `fsutil.write_file_json("settings.json", {"theme": "dark", "language": "zh"})`
137	- `lines = fsutil.read_file_lines("large_file.txt", line_start=10, line_end=20)`
138	- `fsutil.get_file_hash("important_file.txt", func="sha256")`
139	- batch ops: `fsutil.delete_files("f1","f2","f3")`, `fsutil.delete_dirs("d1","d2","d3")`
140	- `fsutil.search_files("project/", pattern="**/*.py")`
141	- test example: `fsutil.split_filepath("dir1/dir2/file.txt")` -> `("dir1/dir2", "file.txt")`
